source.title: MUST HAVE Mid-Round LEAGUE WINNERS in 2026 Fantasy Football

methodology: League Winner candidates combine source-attributed upside research with the site's league-adjusted opportunity-cost model. The model weights price-adjusted value over replacement (25%), role-expansion probability (20%), 80th-percentile Monte Carlo ceiling (15%), sustainable efficiency (15%), offense and line environment (10%), durability and expected availability (10%), and market confirmation (5%). The orange tag is a watchlist signal, not a guarantee and not an automatic replacement for league rank, current ADP, injury status, roster need, or confirmed-keeper availability.

candidates.thesis: The presenters view Swift as an efficient RB3 whose 2025 production was surprisingly close to Saquon Barkley's despite 57 fewer carries.
candidates.evidence: 1,087 rushing yards, 34 receptions, 10 total touchdowns, 5.4 yards per touch and 14.3 fantasy points per game; top-20 in yards after contact and missed tackles forced, and top-10 in runs of 10-plus and 15-plus yards.
candidates.risk: Backfield touches may remain split, so the case depends on efficiency and Chicago's offensive environment rather than workhorse volume.

candidates.thesis: The cheaper half of a projected committee offers weekly flex value and RB3 upside without paying the larger uncertainty premium attached to TreVeyon Henderson.
candidates.evidence: Third in yards after contact per attempt, fifth in avoided tackles per attempt and third in fantasy points per touch among running backs; the transcript also cites strong receiving efficiency.
candidates.risk: A true committee could cap weekly volume, and the receiving split remains uncertain.

candidates.thesis: Warren is priced as an RB3 despite an RB16 finish and a receiving profile that can keep him productive in a split backfield.
candidates.evidence: The transcript cites 53 avoided tackles, 1.58 yards per route run and a blind comparison that closely matched Breece Hall while Warren remained roughly three rounds cheaper.
candidates.risk: Rico Dowdle and the new staff could prevent a clean lead-back role.

candidates.thesis: Vacated targets and an established connection with Daniel Jones give Warren a realistic path from TE5 to a top-two positional finish.
candidates.evidence: As a rookie he led Indianapolis with 112 targets and produced 82 touches, 825 yards and five touchdowns; the presenters project that approximately 130 targets could produce roughly 100 catches and 1,100 yards.
candidates.risk: The ceiling depends on target concentration and the health and effectiveness of the Colts passing game.

candidates.thesis: Moore becomes Josh Allen's projected alpha receiver and reunites with Joe Brady, creating a rebound path well above his fifth-round price.
candidates.evidence: From 2019 through 2024 Moore averaged 135 targets and more than 1,100 receiving yards; his best season came with Brady calling plays, while Allen previously supported elite Stefon Diggs volume.
candidates.risk: Buffalo can distribute targets broadly if Moore does not clearly separate from the rest of the receiving group.

candidates.thesis: A versatile, expanding role could make Washington Jacksonville's most frequently used receiver even if his formal depth-chart label remains fluid.
candidates.evidence: The transcript cites a six-catch, 118-yard, one-touchdown first-team scrimmage and 25 targets of 20-plus yards in 2025, fifth most in the NFL.
candidates.risk: His ADP has already climbed sharply, and Brian Thomas Jr. and Jakobi Meyers can keep the target hierarchy competitive.

candidates.thesis: Brooks offers the cheaper side of Carolina's backfield with a plausible path to the lead role once fully reintegrated.
candidates.evidence: The presenters point to his college pedigree, pass-catching use in camp, explosiveness and the possibility that he reaches Week 1 roughly 21 months removed from surgery.
candidates.risk: Two ACL procedures, a possible four-to-six-week ramp-up and Chuba Hubbard's contract make this the highest medical-risk target in the group.

candidates.thesis: The presenters believe Wilson's late-2025 breakout and projected 'Puka role' create top-12 upside at an eighth-round acquisition cost.
candidates.evidence: They cite 126 targets, 78 catches, more than 1,000 yards, seven touchdowns and a WR2 overall stretch from Week 11 onward.
candidates.risk: Other analysts expect target regression with Marvin Harrison Jr. healthy, so this tag intentionally coexists with the site's contrary expert-fade research.

candidates.thesis: The league model sees one of the board's largest price-adjusted running-back ceilings: starter-level VORP at a cost roughly 30 picks later than his modeled rank.
candidates.evidence: Current full-PPR model: rank 50, ADP 79.7, 11.6 projected PPG, 7.4 PPG over replacement and an injury-risk score of 12. His receiving profile creates a three-down path if his workload expands.
candidates.risk: A current leg issue and a potentially shared backfield keep this from being a volume guarantee; verify pre-draft health and role reports.

candidates.thesis: A first-round rookie with a newly opened workload path offers immediate redraft upside and unusually strong future keeper leverage in the NYFL.
candidates.evidence: Current full-PPR model: rank 53, ADP 70.0, 11.4 projected PPG, 7.2 PPG over replacement and an injury-risk score of 12. Seattle's changed backfield raises both his touch ceiling and the probability of a second-half featured role.
candidates.risk: The workload has not been proven in regular-season games, and a committee or pass-protection limitations could delay the breakout.

source.title: Seattle Seahawks running back depth chart and 2026 fantasy outlook

candidates.thesis: The model's combination of mid-round price, receiving utility and starter-level VORP gives Tuten a realistic route to an RB1 return without an RB1 acquisition cost.
candidates.evidence: Current full-PPR model: rank 45, ADP 63.8, 12.1 projected PPG, 7.9 PPG over replacement and an injury-risk score of 13. His profile remains one of the strongest price-versus-ceiling combinations outside the early rounds.
candidates.risk: Jacksonville lists Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. as co-starters, so uncertain goal-line and early-down shares widen the outcome range.

source.title: Tuten and Rodriguez listed as co-starters

candidates.thesis: A young receiver with a plausible path to become his offense's leading target can beat a WR3 acquisition cost by multiple tiers if the breakout arrives quickly.
candidates.evidence: Current full-PPR model: rank 59, ADP 76.9, 11.9 projected PPG, 4.4 PPG over replacement and an injury-risk score of 13. Age, target-growth potential and keeper carryover make the ceiling more valuable than the median alone suggests.
candidates.risk: Target competition and normal rookie volatility can produce an uneven first half, so price discipline remains important.

candidates.thesis: Fannin's route to a team-leading target share creates the kind of inexpensive positional advantage that can separate a roster at tight end.
candidates.evidence: Current full-PPR model: rank 74, ADP 71.4, 11.1 projected PPG, 3.1 PPG over replacement, live Tier 2 and an injury-risk score of 14. NFL.com also identified him as a top-10 league-winner candidate after a TE6 rookie season and a clearer 2026 target path.
candidates.risk: The market already prices in part of the breakout, and Cleveland's passing volume may limit the absolute ceiling if targets remain distributed.
